title: Uncertainty Drives Social Bias Changes in Quantized Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating changes in stereotypical vs. anti-stereotypical choice probabilities, equalized odds differences in decision contexts (Adult, Credit datasets), and toxicity/safety rates in open-ended generation before and after quantization.
Measuring response flips in multiple-choice stereotyping datasets (e.g., BBQ, StereoSet) and measuring safe vs. biased text generation across racial groups using automated safety classifiers.
Assessing equalized odds in decision-making scenarios and evaluating word/stereotype associations using datasets like BBQ, IAT, and Credit.
Evaluating safe vs. unsafe generation and stereotypical word associations targeting different religious identities using datasets like IAT, StereoSet, and CEB.
Measuring stereotype associations and safe text generation using word pairing (IAT) and ambiguous context datasets (BBQ, FMT10K).
Using multiple-choice and open-ended generation datasets (BBQ, BiasLens) to measure stereotype rates against low-income individuals or specific socioeconomic statuses.
Evaluated via BBQ and BiasLens by checking for response flips in stereotyping multiple-choice questions and analyzing open-ended generations for toxicity.
Evaluated using BBQ and BiasLens through multiple-choice and open-ended stereotyping prompts comparing different national origins.
Evaluated via BBQ, BiasLens, and FMT10K for stereotype and toxicity rates regarding body size and physical appearance.
Evaluated via StereoSet and BiasLens by measuring the probability of models choosing stereotypical continuations or associations related to specific professions.
